document_title: Batch Zero, and the calendar with a hole in it

S1.dek: ERCOT set itself a date to tell service providers how every large load was classified. That date passed 12 days ago.

S2.quote: "ERCOT will not notify each Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider and Transmission Service Provider of how any Large Load is classified in the Batch Zero Interconnection Study by August 7, 2026"

S3.kick: "Update Regarding Batch Zero Timelines and Processes"
S3.qn: No service provider was told how any large load was classified.

S4.quote: "The extent to which data centers are bringing their own water and reusing their own water as opposed to using water needed by local communities."
S4.src: Directive to the PUCT and ERCOT · c15

S5.o1: of requests to connect to the Texas grid
S5.o2: of the new power requests are data centers
S5.o3: Texas' record peak electricity demand for ERCOT

S6.hook: One office. The same day. Two wordings.
S6.q1: "The PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward."
S6.q2: "before any additional data centers are approved to move forward"
S6.foot: The signed letter words it more narrowly than the press release does. Both are on the record and they are not interchangeable.

S7.lead: The sector said it will comply.
S7.quote: "I established clear guardrails to ensure data centers protect our electric grid, conserve our water, respect our neighborhoods, and pay their own way ..."
S7.src: Office of the Governor, August 18th · c18

S8.quote: "One data center that could not comply chose to end operations before even beginning construction."
S8.src: Office of the Governor, August 18th · c17

S9.rows: ERCOT said it would file for a good cause exception ahead of the August 20th, 2026 open meeting, and said it would update the notice once the filing is made.
S9.lab: ERCOT market notice. August 20th, 2026, 1 day out. Planning Guide Sections 5 and 9.
